method: logistic regression, Wald test on the year slope
note: Odds ratio below 1 means batting first has become less successful over time.

hypothesis: ODI: first-innings totals do not change with year
method: OLS regression slope (runs per year); Spearman rho as a robustness check
note: R2=0.074; Spearman rho=0.26 (p=1.29e-05); DLS-affected matches excluded because their first innings can be shortened.

hypothesis: T20: first-innings totals do not change with year
method: OLS regression slope (runs per year); Spearman rho as a robustness check
note: R2=0.002; Spearman rho=0.10 (p=0.0616); DLS-affected matches excluded because their first innings can be shortened.

hypothesis: ODI: the chasing side's win probability does not depend on the target
method: logistic regression, Wald test (target in units of 10 runs)
effect_name: odds ratio per +10 runs of target
note: A strongly negative slope is the expected sanity check: bigger targets are harder.

hypothesis: T20: the chasing side's win probability does not depend on the target
method: logistic regression, Wald test (target in units of 10 runs)
effect_name: odds ratio per +10 runs of target
note: A strongly negative slope is the expected sanity check: bigger targets are harder.

hypothesis: ODI: first-innings totals have the same distribution at every ground
method: Kruskal-Wallis across 12 grounds with >= 6 matches
note: Not adjusted for year or team strength, so part of the effect is era, not ground.

hypothesis: T20: first-innings totals have the same distribution at every ground
method: Kruskal-Wallis across 28 grounds with >= 6 matches
note: Not adjusted for year or team strength, so part of the effect is era, not ground.
